scenario: A 33-year-old G1P0 female at 32 weeks gestation presents after a high-speed MVC with altered level of consciousness, hypotension, left tension pneumothorax/hemothorax, pelvic instability, fetal distress, and need for trauma resuscitation, chest decompression/tube thoracostomy, transfusion, and intubation.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Let's get a liter of normal saline in wide open — she's hypotensive at 80/50 and tachy at 155.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Normal saline 1 liter bolus is up and running wide open.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a bedside FAST now — she's in shock and I need to look for free fluid.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: FAST is back: no pericardial effusion, but positive free fluid in the abdomen. She's still unstable — 79/51, HR 158, sat 88 on the non-rebreather, RR 40, GCS 9.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Activate the massive transfusion protocol and hang 2 units of packed red cells now. She's still in shock after the liter of saline with free fluid in the belly — this is hemorrhage.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting massive transfusion protocol — hanging 2 units packed red cells now. I'll keep them coming and monitor vitals.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Set up for RSI now — GCS is 9 and she can't protect her airway, and she's only satting 88 on the non-rebreather. Preoxygenate with the BVM and draw up the RSI meds while the blood keeps running.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: RSI meds drawn up and ready, BVM ventilating now. Suction and tube confirmed at bedside. Ready when you are.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Push the RSI meds and let's intubate now — she's not protecting her airway and only satting 85. Confirm tube placement with EtCO2 and auscultation once it's in, keep the blood running.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Intubation complete. RSI meds given, patient was bagged prior to the attempt, tube's in.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 units of plasma now to keep the massive transfusion going in a balanced ratio — she's still hypotensive and tachy with free fluid in the belly. Keep the blood coming and get surgery to the bedside now for source control.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hanging 2 units plasma per massive transfusion protocol now. I'll keep the products coming and update you on the ratio.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 more units of packed red cells now, continuing the massive transfusion protocol — she's still hypotensive and tachy with free fluid in the belly. Run it through a fluid warmer, she's cold. And where the hell is surgery? I need them at the bedside for source control now.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting massive transfusion protocol — 2 units packed RBCs going in now. I'll keep the products coming and monitor for transfusion reaction.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 1 unit of platelets now to keep the ratio balanced — she's still tachy at 130 with free fluid in the belly. Run it through the warmer, her temp's 35. And I need surgery at the bedside now for source control.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 more units of packed cells through the warmer now, keep the massive transfusion going — she's still tachy at 126 and cold at 35 with free fluid in the belly. I need surgery at the bedside this minute for source control.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting massive transfusion protocol, 2 units packed red cells going up now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: She's still only satting 88% on the vent at 100% oxygen. Bump the PEEP up to 10 to recruit and improve her oxygenation, then recheck the sat and confirm equal breath sounds bilaterally.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a bedside obstetric ultrasound now — she's a reproductive-age woman with free fluid in the belly, and I need to know if she's pregnant and whether there's an obstetric source of bleeding. It changes our surgical priorities.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Bedside OB ultrasound back: positive fetal heart activity, she's pregnant. Sat's up slightly to 89% on PEEP 10, HR 117, BP 101/65, temp still 35.4.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Two more units of packed cells through the warmer now, keep the massive transfusion going — she's still tachy at 117 and cold at 35.4 with free fluid in the belly. And she's pregnant with fetal heart activity confirmed — I need surgery at the bedside this minute for source control.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Starting massive transfusion protocol, hanging 2 units packed red cells now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Start norepinephrine now to support her pressure while the transfusion keeps running — she's still hypotensive and tachy at 102 with free fluid in the belly. And I need surgery at the bedside this minute for source control.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Norepinephrine is up and running.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Hang 2 units of plasma through the warmer now to keep the massive transfusion ratio balanced — she's still bleeding with free fluid in the belly and cold at 35.6. I need surgery at the bedside now for source control.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Hanging 2 units plasma now per massive transfusion protocol. I'll keep the products coming and let you know as they're in.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a portable pelvis film now — she's got free fluid in the belly and I need to rule out a pelvic fracture as a bleeding source.
